title: Specific charge expression
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be the correct expression for e/m, derived from equating Lorentz force to centripetal force in the magnetic field.

title: Y-coordinate range
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must correctly state the range of y-coordinates (0 to 2a) from which electrons can exit the magnetic field and enter the electric field.

title: Maximum distance on screen
description: Essential: The final answer for part (3) must be the correct maximum distance (9a/4) from point Q on the fluorescent screen.

title: Magnetic geometry analysis
description: Important: The solution must correctly use the given trajectory through point O to determine the radius of circular motion (r = a) and the geometry of the triangle region.

title: Electric field kinematics
description: Important: The solution must correctly apply kinematics in the electric field (constant acceleration along y) to find the exit position and angle as functions of entry y-coordinate.

title: Optimization for maximum
description: Important: For part (3), the solution must combine the exit conditions to form an expression for the distance H(y) and find its maximum (e.g., via derivative or completing the square).

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The working should demonstrate dimensional consistency, especially when combining magnetic and electric field equations.

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall: Penalize sign errors in the Lorentz force direction, electric field acceleration (positive y), or incorrect trigonometric signs for the exit angle.

title: Incorrect radius or geometry
description: Pitfall: Penalize incorrectly identifying the cyclotron radius from the given trajectory or misinterpreting the boundaries of the magnetic field region.
